consensus_summary: Biblical 'to know' (yadaʿ/ginōskō) primarily denotes intimate, experiential, relational/covenantal knowledge—especially personal communion with God—rather than mere intellectual awareness; sub-senses include the sexual euphemism of marital intimacy, divine election/recognition, and knowledge evidenced by obedience/love.
book_summary: Covenant relationship proven by obedience, illustrated by the intimate marital 'knew' and by the idea that a stranger is one not known.
rationale: The book's core claim (relational covenant knowledge with marital intimacy and the 'I never knew you' contrast) is fully covered by the consensus primary meaning and its standard alternatives. It is refined rather than a pure match because it materially narrows and sharpens the broad relational consensus into a single definitional package that foregrounds 'proven by obedience' as constitutive and tightly equates the whole to the marriage idiom plus the stranger motif.
strongest_objection: One could argue MATCH on the ground that every element (marriage intimacy, obedience proof, stranger contrast) already appears inside the consensus primary-plus-alternatives cluster, so the book merely restates rather than refines.
